The aircraft, a CL60 with registration number T7-SEI and flight identification DWC052, was departing Abuja for the Murtala Muhammed International Airport, Lagos, when the incident occurred. According to a serious incident report, the aircraft took off from Runway 22 at 4:17 p.m. Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) and, about three nautical miles from the airport, was climbing at 3,000 feet when the crew issued a distress call at 4:20 p.m.

stories.title: Repressive, secretive and highly militarised: Eritrea, the east African country facing UK visa ban threat
stories.summary: People on a busy street in Asmara, Eritrea’s capital, in June. Photograph: Monicah Mwangi/Reuters View image in fullscreen People on a busy street in Asmara, Eritrea’s capital, in June. Photograph: Monicah Mwangi/Reuters Explainer Repressive, secretive and highly militarised: Eritrea, the east African country facing UK visa ban threat Country has not had an election in 33 years and has withdrawn cooperation with UK on migrant returns Eritrea, the east African country embroiled in a row with the UK over its refusal to accept the return of rejected asylum seekers and criminals, is considered one of world’s most secretive and repressive states, with reports of arbitrary detention and severe restrictions on freedom of expression, opinion and religion. Situated in the Horn of Africa and bordering Sudan, Ethiopia and Djibouti, it became a sovereign state after gaining independence from Ethiopia in 1993 following a 30-year war. The country is run by an authoritarian regime under Isaias Afwerki, who led separatist forces to defeat Ethiopian forces in 1991 and became president in 1993.

stories.title: Tim Jeal obituary
stories.summary: Henry Morton Stanley's expedition crossing the Makata swamp in central Africa in 1871, in search of David Livingstone. Photograph: Chronicle/Alamy View image in fullscreen Henry Morton Stanley's expedition crossing the Makata swamp in central Africa in 1871, in search of David Livingstone. Photograph: Chronicle/Alamy Obituary Tim Jeal obituary Biographer who altered perceptions of Henry Morton Stanley, David Livingstone, Robert Baden-Powell and other figures active in Africa Thanks to the biographer and novelist Tim Jeal, who has died aged 81, we now know that one of the most famous sentences in journalism – “Dr Livingstone, I presume?” – was almost certainly never uttered. In November 1871, after a 700-mile expedition, the Welsh-American journalist and adventurer Henry Morton Stanley tracked down David Livingstone, the Scottish missionary and explorer. He had been lost to the outside world for six years and was now nearing death, in Ujiji, on the shores of Lake Tanganyika in present-day Tanzania.

stories.title: A Madagascar, l’ascension de l’ambitieux colonel Michaël Randrianirina
stories.summary: « Madagascar, un an après le coup d’Etat » (2/4). Depuis son arrivée au pouvoir, le « colonel Michaël » tente de rassurer ses partenaires et multiplie les promesses aux Malgaches, dans l’optique du scrutin présidentiel attendu d’ici à novembre 2027. Des observateurs indépendants alertent toutefois sur une opposition et une justice muselées.

stories.title: Aérien : avec la reprise de TAP, Lufthansa peut-il bousculer Air France-KLM en Afrique ?
stories.summary: Avec une offre de 1,2 milliard d’euros, Lufthansa intègre le capital de TAP Air Portugal. Une prise de participation qui lui ouvre grand les portes du marché lusophone en Afrique et renforce sa présence face à Air France-KLM.

stories.title: Pétrole : Le Nigeria cherche à devenir un pôle régional de raffinage
stories.summary: Le Nigeria, le premier producteur africain de pétrole, cherche à devenir un pôle régional de raffinage. La flambée du brut et les pénuries d'approvisionnement causé par la fermeture du détroit d'Ormuz a poussé de nombreux pays a se tourner vers la raffinerie du milliardaire Aliko Dangote. Reportage au cœur de cette raffinerie.

stories.title: Cancer du sein au Sénégal : le coût des mammographies, un frein au dépistage
stories.summary: Au Sénégal, le cancer du sein est le cancer le plus fréquent chez les femmes. FRANCE 24 a rencontré la présidente de la Ligue sénégalaise contre le cancer, Fatma Guenoune.

stories.title: Popular Nigerian gospel singer Toluwanisings dies aged 41
stories.summary: Image source, Toluwanisings Image caption, Toluwanisings' family appealed to fans to remember them in prayer during this period of mourning By Mansur Abubakar Reporting from Abuja Published 15 October 2026 One of Nigeria's most popular gospel singers, Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, known as Toluwanisings, has died, his family has announced. In a statement posted on the deceased's Instagram page, the family said the singer had "said goodbye to the world" in the early hours of Wednesday, 14 October. They also appealed to fans to remember his wife, children and family in prayer during this period of mourning. The family said burial arrangements would be announced in due course. Toluwanisings was known for his beautiful voice and energetic praise performances that encouraged audience participation, according to some of the tributes paid by his fans on social media.

stories.title: Ceuta : des ONG accusent l’armée espagnole de « cruauté » à l’égard des migrants et dénoncent le non-respect de leurs droits fondamentaux
stories.summary: Au moment où le roi Felipe VI visitait la ville nord-africaine, mardi, huit ONG ont annoncé la saisine du défenseur du peuple espagnol pour dénoncer l’opacité entourant les retours prétendument volontaires vers le Maroc.

stories.title: Mauritius reels from worst riots in decades after woman shot by police
stories.summary: Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Mauritius is a well known as a tourism and financial services hub By Basillioh Rukanga Published 14 October 2026 Updated 15 October 2026 Police in Mauritius imposed an overnight curfew overnight to quell the worst riots to break out on the Indian Ocean island in decades. Protests over water shortages and the high cost of living that started a week ago erupted into violence on Friday when a woman was shot and wounded by police at a roadblock. The circumstances of the shooting are not clear, but the officer has since been arrested and remanded in custody. Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam ordered the curfew on Tuesday, warning against those "acting against the interests of the country", which is a tourism and financial services hub. "Those who have carried out these actions will have to face the very heavy consequences warranted by their anti-patriotic acts," he said in an address to the nation. The government said it was extending the curfew until Friday morning as part of the measures agreed on during a special cabinet meeting on Wednesday.

stories.title: LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested
stories.summary: HRW said arrests had been made based on information found on phones, third-party allegations or raids on private premises, while lawyers fear representing those detained. Photograph: AP View image in fullscreen HRW said arrests had been made based on information found on phones, third-party allegations or raids on private premises, while lawyers fear representing those detained. Photograph: AP LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reports Mass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a new report . More than 320 individuals have been arrested and detained on allegations of “acts against nature” since February, according to HIV Justice Network , an organisation quoted in the Human Rights Watch (HRW) report. Among these, at least 84 were charged with “voluntary HIV transmission”, solely on the basis of their HIV status.

stories.title: Tradition festive ou "crime" : pourquoi les "bouquets d'argent" font-ils polémique en Afrique ?
stories.summary: Sept femmes arrêtées début octobre au Ghana sont accusées d'avoir confectionné des "bouquets d'argent", fabriqués avec de vrais billets de banque et destinés à la vente. Un cadeau tendance lors des mariages, anniversaires et autres cérémonies dans le pays, mais considéré dans plusieurs États africains comme une atteinte à la souveraineté monétaire.

stories.title: « Les Damnés de la donnée » : les travailleurs du Sud, invisibilisés et pourtant indispensables au développement de l’IA
stories.summary: Au fil d’une enquête menée auprès d’annotateurs de données à Madagascar, le sociologue Clément Le Ludec met en lumière la centralité du travail de cette main-d’œuvre précarisée et invisibilisée, indispensable au bon fonctionnement des systèmes d’intelligence artificielle.

stories.title: Africa: African Development Bank and UNDP Advance Ai 10 Billion Initiative to Turn Africa's Ai Potential Into Productivity
stories.summary: African Development Bank and UNDP Advance Ai 10 Billion Initiative to Turn Africa's Ai Potential Into Productivity 14 October 2026 Content from a Premium Partner African Development Bank (Abidjan) The AI 10 Billion Initiative has received a boost following a visit by a delegation from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) to the African Development Bank Group to move from launch to delivery. The AI 10 Billion Initiative is a co-designed partnership between the Bank Group, UNDP and private sector partners. By orchestrating $1 billion per year over the next decade, the initiative can contribute to 25 million new jobs by 2035. The UNDP Regional Bureau for Africa's delegation was led by Keyzom Ngodup Massally, Director of the AI Hub for Sustainable Development along with UNDP Platform for Investment and Technical Assistance (PISTA). The mission follows the initiative's launch at the Nairobi AI Forum in February 2026 , and the ongoing implementation of the Africa Accelerator for Digital Public Infrastructure (AA4DPI) initiative.

stories.title: Ebola: le Kenya durcit ses mesures de prévention après un deuxième cas sur son sol
stories.summary: Ebola: le Kenya durcit ses mesures de prévention après un deuxième cas sur son sol Le ministère de la Santé a annoncé mercredi soir, une seconde personne déclarée sur le territoire kényan. Il s’agit d’un proche du premier malade décédé la semaine passée. Le patient était déjà en quarantaine lorsque ses symptômes se sont déclarés. Les autorités kényanes assurent que la situation est sous contrôle. Mais pour qu’elle le reste, le ministre de la Santé, a signé deux ordonnances en début de semaine pour mettre en place de nouvelles mesures sanitaires.

stories.summary: Simbarashe Kundizeza says the story is entirely his own work. View image in fullscreen Simbarashe Kundizeza says the story is entirely his own work. Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza denies using AI to write prize-winning story Article in Atlantic claims The Blue Fighter was artificially generated, days after it won Caine prize for African writers The Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has denied using AI to write a prize-winning short story after an article in the Atlantic said software had flagged it as almost completely AI-generated. Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter was announced as the winner of the prestigious Caine prize for African writers on 6 October. Five days later, The Atlantic published an article by the author and journalist Vauhini Vara titled: “Yet Another Literary prize winner Seems to Be AI.” Vara said that she had run the story through the AI-detection software Pangram, which itself uses AI, and it had deemed the story to be almost completely artificially generated.

stories.title: Kenya confirms second Ebola case - a relative of the first victim
stories.summary: Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, The Ebola virus spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit By Lucy Fleming Published 14 October 2026 Kenya has confirmed a second case of Ebola, 10 days after a businessman died of the virus after he had travelled to the East African nation from the Democratic Republic of Congo. The new patient, a 39-year-old man, is a close relative of the first case and was already in quarantine when he fell ill on Tuesday, Kenya's health ministry says. The incubation period for Ebola ranges from two to 21 days, meaning those exposed to the virus may not become ill for several weeks. Detecting his illness early had improved his chances of recovery and limited the chance of him passing the virus on to others, the ministry said, as it urged the public to "stay calm but vigilant". "Both cases are linked, and there is no evidence of spread in the wider community," the ministry said. "Kenya remains open, with no restrictions on travel, trade or public gatherings", it added. Questions remain over Ebola patient who travelled across three nations undetected Published 7 days ago The 40-year-old Kenyan man who died on 5 October was diagnosed with Ebola shortly after being admitted to hospital in the capital, Nairobi.

stories.summary: Image source, Press Association Image caption, Antoine Semenyo was playing for Bournemouth when the alleged incident happened during a match against Liverpool in August 2025 Published 14 October 2026 Footballer Antoine Semenyo "froze" after he was allegedly racially abused by a Liverpool fan during a Premier League match at Anfield, a court has heard. The Manchester City winger, who was playing for Bournemouth at the time, was preparing to take a throw-in when Mark Mogan, 47, allegedly shouted a racist insult at him on 15 August 2025. Prosecutors said Semenyo was "clearly hurt and upset" and reported the incident to referee Anthony Taylor when the ball next went out of play. Mogan, of Dovecot, Liverpool, denies racially aggravated behaviour. Photograph: Phanie/Sipa Press/Alamy Guinea-Bissau denies it has approved controversial vaccine trial in newborns Health minister says government ‘did not authorize’ Danish-led hepatitis B trial in babies backed by RFK Jr Guinea-Bissau has not approved the controversial hepatitis B study in newborns that would be funded by the US government and private partners, the African country’s minister of health said on Tuesday. The study, which would not investigate the safety or effectiveness of vaccines but would instead track “nonspecific” health outcomes like overall mortality or neurodevelopmental conditions, has been championed by Robert F Kennedy Jr , secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime anti-vaccine activist. stories.summary: Publicité Navi Pillay, prix Nobel de la paix : l'accusation de génocide contre Israël "repose sur des faits" Afrique La juriste sud-africaine Navi Pillay, lauréate du prix Nobel de la paix, a accordé une interview à RFI dans laquelle elle retrace son parcours au sein de la justice internationale et défend le travail de la commission d'enquête indépendante de l'ONU sur Gaza. Publié le : 14/10/2026 - 12:02 Modifié le : 14/10/2026 - 14:59 3 min Temps de lecture Partager Par : Olivier BRAS Navi Pillay s'exprime lors du Forum de Nuremberg, le vendredi 9 octobre 2026, après avoir été désignée lauréate du prix Nobel de la paix 2026. © Daniel Karmann/DPA via AP La lauréate du Nobel de la paix cette année "a œuvré pour garantir que les crimes de guerre, les crimes contre l'humanité et les génocides soient poursuivis", a rappelé le Comité en attribuant la prestigieuse récompense, le 9 octobre, à la juriste sud-africai ne Navanethem Pillay, dite Navi Pillay . Elle est revenue dans une interview diffusée le 14 octobre par RFI sur son travail à la tête d'une commission d'enquête indépendante de l'ONU qui avait accusé, l'an dernier, Israël de commettre un génocide dans la bande de Gaza et sur les nombreuses attaques qui visent encore le territoire. "Je maintiens ma position parce qu'il ne s’agit pas simplement d’une opinion que j’avance. stories.title: Mourners killed by Kenya police at Odinga national farewell not part of violence, BBC finds
stories.summary: Figure caption, "There were so many people, why him?" Yvonne Akinyi remembers the day her husband was shot dead Published 12 October 2026 Three mourners killed when Kenyan police opened fire at a national farewell for former Prime Minister Raila Odinga were not involved in a clash that sparked gunfire, a BBC Africa Eye investigation has found. During an event held last October for people to pay their respects to Odinga, three people were shot dead after mourners attempted to gain access to the VIP section of Nairobi's Kasarani Stadium by force. BBC analysis from inside the stadium shows the victims were each between at least 60m (197 ft) and 160m from the scuffles. Kenya's Interior Minister Kipchumba Murkomen told the BBC that the police action had been "restrained" after the crowd starting throwing stones. In footage analysed by the BBC, it is clear that objects, including plastic chairs, are thrown, but we have no evidence that they included stones.
